original.guitar: Jeff Cook (guitar and fiddle, arranger of the song)
original.amp: Not documented. Early-80s Nashville studio country: clean Fender-style amp, compressed
original.effects: Compressor, short slapback, plate reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: Lead single from The Closer You Get (January 1983). No source documents the guitar gear on this song.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the clean, bright, driving rhythm under the fiddle. Channel B adds tweed grit for the louder sections. Keep the strumming tight and accent the backbeat. The fiddle carries the main melody.
recipes.why: Early-80s Nashville records used a clean, compressed Fender-style sound with a short slapback and a studio plate reverb. A split bridge pickup gives the Tele-like snap.

original.guitar: Jeff Cook (guitar and fiddle, arranger of the song)
original.amp: Not documented. Early-80s Nashville studio country: clean Fender-style amp, compressed
original.effects: Compressor, light chorus, delay, plate reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: Lead single from The Closer You Get (January 1983). No source documents the guitar gear on this song.

recipes.tips: Channel A for clean, snappy country licks (hybrid picking, double stops, pedal-steel-style bends). Channel B for a fatter solo with a little tweed breakup. The light chorus is the early-80s touch. Turn it off for a more traditional sound.
recipes.why: Early-80s country leads were clean and compressed for sustain, with a hint of chorus and a delay just behind the notes. Channel B adds tweed breakup for a fatter solo.
